sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Hill (1942) retains the combination Mirotermes sunteri Hill, 1927, with the type locality Darwin, Northern Territory. The alate is distinctly smaller than M. quadratus and larger than M. melvillensis, and can be distinguished from the other species by the shape of the pronotum; the soldier is closest to M. harrisi and can be distinguished by its short, stout, slightly curved frontal tubercles, its poorly developed lateral tubercles and its hairy fontanelle area.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Distinctly smaller than M. quadratus and larger than M. melvillensis. Head, pronotum, the anterior third of the mesothorax and metathorax and the proximal abdominal tergites dark chestnut, the remaining tergites and the pleurites a lighter brown; wings smoky, as in M. cheeli. Head and pronotum hairy. Compound eyes with a transparent rim, not very prominent, variable in size. Ocelli broadly oval, separated from the compound eyes by about their short diameter, the inner margin slightly raised. Fontanelle linear, narrow, longer than the ocellus. Postclypeus about half as long as wide (0.22×0.44—0.24×0.44). The large apical tooth of the mandibles is far from the adjacent tooth. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 usually the shortest and narrowest; segments 4 and 5 usually equal in length. Pronotum (Fig. 313) very large relative to the head, usually wider than the head, about more than a third longer than wide, the anterior margin concave, the sides sloping rather steeply down to a narrowly rounded posterior margin. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum deeply concave. Measurements: length with wings 9.25—10.00; length without wings 5.00—5.25; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.05—1.13; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.66—0.73; head width 0.91—1.00; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.25—0.29; ocellus length 0.09—0.11; pronotum length 0.61—0.71; pronotum width 0.95—1.00; fore wing length 7.50; fore wing width 2.00.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head orange yellow, with sparse long hairs. Labrum slightly longer than wide, the sides parallel, the anterior angles almost always extended into sharp projections, sometimes slightly bilobed. Frontal tubercles short, stout, hairy, not sharply upcurved; lateral tubercles poorly developed. Mandibles very long and slender, far longer than the head capsule. Many golden hairs around the fontanelle. Antennae 14-segmented; segments 2—5 very variable, segment 4 often the shortest, segment 2 slightly longer, segment 3 longer than segment 2 and shorter than segment 5, the remaining segments long and narrow (Fig. 314). Measurements: total length 6.15—6.30; head length (including mandibles) 3.48—3.85; head length (to apex of frontal tubercles) 1.43—1.71; head width 1.02—1.15; pronotum length 0.34—0.44; pronotum width 0.68—0.77.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942). The heading line was OCRed with the author set as "Kill" (that is, Hill). The original does not describe the worker here (the worker of the 1927 original description is not repeated), so no worker section is provided.
